quest.title: "The Seventh Samurai"
quest.description: Xavier seems to be bothered by a certain matter...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x2, Mora x20000

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Wait! Ah, Sir Soldier, the line you just read lacks the right emotional gravitas.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: "Samurai, like the wind sweeping the earth."

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Do you still remember what I said about the play? It is supposed to feel liberating and give the audience a sense of the vicissitudes of life. I said liberating! Liberating, you understand?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: This line is key to the whole play. You must express your emotions completely, fully, and perfectly!

dialogues.speaker: Toranosuke
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Moreover, don't swing your sword in such haste... Make sure you are in view, otherwise, the Film Kamera will not be able to capture your movements at all.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Pose, and then pause, okay? Stop for a moment, then slice downwards with great force.

dialogues.speaker: Toranosuke
dialogues.text: But you can't swing your sword like that when you fight against people...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: True, but you have to tailor your acting to the production's needs.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well then. Please ready up, and we shall give this another go...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Oh, it's you! Ah, my dear {F#girl}{M#boy}, a fair wind must have blown you here.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: As you can see, I'm shooting a swashbuckler film with our good soldier here. I call it "The Seventh Samurai."

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Oh, "swashbuckler film" is what I'm calling films of this genre.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: This sort of film shall have sword-fighting scenes, and it shall take the viewers on an incredible journey across the battlefield... Well, that's the idea, at least!

choices.text: To think that Mr. Toranosuke would have time...

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: This activity has been approved by our superiors. According to them, it will help to increase the Shogunate's prestige.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: That said, I haven't a clue how Mr. Xavier managed to convince them...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Honestly, Mr. Mikoshi Genjirou is such a... serious man. Fortunately, he is also most understanding.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: After I had a sincere talk with him, he accepted my request quite happily.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But... In exchange, I have to make a movie that has to do with the Shogunate, preferably with a samurai as the protagonist.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I was always interested in this sort of subject matter anyway, so of course, I agreed to it, and Lord Mikoshi Genjirou was also very pleased.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: In addition to personally appointing our good soldier to go with me, he also assigned some skilled troops to me, and then he said...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: "Use these scenes of steel clashing against steel to display the majesty of the samurai and the Shogunate."

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I have to say that Mr. Genjirou really is a man of vision, to have grasped the potential of using films as a marketing tool so very quickly...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: And as for me, I will never refuse anything that will help me make my films.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: To be honest, it's not going that well...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: While these soldiers are highly skilled in martial arts, they are not used to this kind of staged fighting.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Not only are their sword movements too fast for the Film Kamera to record, they sometimes even run outside of its view.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Traveler, if you have the time, do you mind following my script and acting the story out for the soldiers to see?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I believe that with your strength and understanding, you will be able to perform brilliantly in front of the Kamera...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: They should be able to better understand the story after watching it from the spectator's point of view.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Come, come! Just read the script and the lines first. This part is mainly about fighting...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah, these are lines from another scene... This one is mainly about fighting, so there aren't that many lines.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, let me take a look at the script.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Oh, by the way, you'll be playing the role of "Juusaburou." Together with several companions, he is employed by the villagers to protect their village...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: In this scene, one of your companions, "Kyuuzou," has lines... I'll play his part, and the two of us will do a reading.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Now, you must embody the role, understand it! Just think of yourself as Juusaburou. Do you understand?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Wonderful! Splendid! Bravo!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Let me know when you are ready. I have to adjust the Film Kamera's position...

choices.text: "But even when imperiled, the samurai is still samurai."
Mind if I play a part?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Of course! Of course! You are, after all, forever a {F#heroine}{M#hero} in my heart!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I'll always remember that "Tatara Tales" that we acted in together.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Although these soldiers are highly skilled in martial arts, they are not used to this kind of staged fighting.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Not only are their sword movements too fast for the Film Kamera to record, they sometimes even run outside of its view.

choices.text: How did you persuade him to help you out?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Come now, our dear soldier understood me just fine. My main job, really, was to persuade Mr. Mikoshi Genjirou to allow me to make a film in Inazuma.

choices.text: "Samurai, like the wind sweeping the earth."

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You said those words with too much passion. It should be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Wonderful, bravo! In that case, let's begin!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I shall make a few adjustments to the Film Kamera and call the soldiers back...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh dear me, this film doesn't seem to have come out right...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Please get ready again, and we shall give it another go.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Wonderful, bravo! In that case, let's begin!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I shall make a few adjustments to the Film Kamera and call the soldiers back...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Perfect! As expected of the {F#heroine}{M#hero} of my heart! A perfect demonstration! You truly are a star!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: A star! That is to say, the most important actor in a film.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Now then, Mr. Soldier. You saw that demonstration clearly, I trust?

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: On the whole, yes. When swinging my blade, I should focus not so much on the "action," itself, but on the "posture," yes?

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: If you only require the "posture"... I have some ideas about that.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Oh? That's wonderful! Please discuss the matter with your fellow soldiers, and we'll do another take in a while.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You have my utmost gratitude for your help, Traveler. Here. These are for you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's the theme of your next film?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The next film, hmm? Well... Actually, I'm quite torn on what its topic should be myself.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Should we do one about the various traditions of the Grand Narukami Shrine? Or the tales of the kitsune and the tanuki?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: There are so many islands here in Inazuma, and so many stories to be told!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But regardless, I have to finish producing "The Seventh Samurai" first.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: If this satisfies those fellows upstairs, I do suspect that future film projects shall progress much more smoothly.

choices.text: Maybe I'd like to change roles next time.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: No problem at all! Once this film has been completed, we should start planning a whole new one.

dialogues.speaker: Toranosuke
dialogues.text: A "swashbuckler film," huh. Mr. Xavier sure does have interesting taste in names.

choices.text: What do you think of these films?

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: Our superiors believe that these films will help to increase the Shogunate's prestige.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: Perhaps I am simply a little slow on the uptake... but I do not see how this is the case.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: This script is full of these... pessimistic lines. There is nothing of samurai dignity here.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: Who knows what they were thinking, that they agreed to all this...

choices.text: How's the situation at the Mikage Furnace?

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: Ever since Sir Hanbei's "promotion," Yousuke has taken over as the person in charge.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: He is a craftsman by birth and trade, and is very down-to-earth and steady. He gets things done, as well.

response.speaker: Toranosuke
response.text: With the Mikage Furnace under his management, I doubt there will be any further problems.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: So, are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not quite ready yet...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well, don't worry. Take your time — just let me know when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean to capture through film?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Aha! That's a fine question. A fine question indeed. But to be honest, I have yet to think it all through, either.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I believe that films can be about anything.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Romance! Suspense! Combat! Even all manner of baseless legends can be the subject of films.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Though I must say that I think films have some sort of charm that I have yet to fully bring out.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Still, I believe that I will find the answer to that question as long as I keep making films.
